content: Diabetes UK is a British charity that focuses on supporting individuals with diabetes, healthcare professionals, and research efforts aimed at improving the lives of those affected by diabetes and ultimately working towards eradicating the condition. The organization was originally established in 1934 under the name The Diabetic Association by H.G. Wells and Dr. R.D. Lawrence. It underwent two name changes: first in 1954 to The British Diabetic Association and later in 2000 to its current name, Diabetes UK. The charity operates a comprehensive website that provides detailed information about diabetes for both healthcare professionals and individuals living with the condition. Diabetes UK has a membership base exceeding 180,000, which includes people with diabetes, their caregivers, and healthcare professionals. The organization established its first voluntary group in 1939, and today, there are approximately 350 such groups across the UK. Additionally, Diabetes UK maintains local offices throughout England and national offices in Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales. The charity organizes conferences for its volunteers and healthcare professionals specializing in diabetes care. It actively campaigns for advancements in the treatment and care of individuals with diabetes. Since the 1930s, Diabetes UK has been running care holidays for children with diabetes, and over time, these have expanded to include family and adult holidays. These holidays are designed to offer support and guidance in a relaxed and enjoyable environment. In 1993, Diabetes UK launched a counseling service called the Careline, which provides support to patients, their families, and friends. The Careline can be accessed via a low-cost phone number, email, or postal correspondence. The organization also maintains an internal library and offers a scientific inquiry service. Diabetes UK funds research within the UK that focuses on understanding the causes of diabetes, improving its treatment, and addressing its complications. The first research grant was awarded in 1936. The charity produces a variety of informational booklets and magazines. For example, Balance, a magazine for patients, was originally published in 1935 under the name The Diabetic Journal and was renamed Balance in 1961. For healthcare professionals, the charity publishes Diabetes Update. Additionally, Diabetes UK collaborates with Blackwell Publishing to produce the academic journal Diabetic Medicine, which was previously published by John Wiley and Sons from its inception in 1984 (Volume 1) until mid-2000 (Volume 17).
